hints.title: Salary Threshold Condition
hints.text: Filter for employees whose salary is strictly less than 30000.

hints.title: Departed Manager Check
hints.text: An employee has a departed manager if manager_id is not null and that manager_id does not exist in the employees table.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT
    employee_id
FROM Employees
WHERE salary < 30000
  AND manager_id IS NOT NULL
  AND manager_id NOT IN (
      SELECT employee_id
      FROM Employees
  )
ORDER BY employee_id ASC;
```

complexity.time: O(N) with an index on employee_id
complexity.space: O(N) space for employee ID subquery set
variables: N: number of employees in Employees table
complexity.notes: Filtering on salary and manager_id NOT IN subquery.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: If manager_id is NULL, omitting the IS NOT NULL check can produce unpredictable NOT IN semantics in SQL.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Explicit manager_id IS NOT NULL condition protects the subquery from three-valued logic pitfalls.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should safely handle NULL manager_id and sort output ascending.

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def find_employees(employees: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    valid_ids = set(employees['employee_id'])
    cond = (
        (employees['salary'] < 30000) &
        (employees['manager_id'].notna()) &
        (~employees['manager_id'].isin(valid_ids))
    )
    res = employees[cond][['employee_id']].sort_values('employee_id')
    return res
solutions.approach: Boolean masking with set membership in pandas
